title: Plan a DigitalOcean managed Postgres with OpenTofu
before_you_start: A personal DigitalOcean account with an API token you can use in the session (plan-only; do not apply).
OpenTofu (`tofu`) is already on the desktop; cluster requirements are in `requirements.md`.

role.title: Platform / DevOps engineer
role.company_context: Product-led SaaS company moving shared data stores onto managed cloud databases. A small platform team owns OpenTofu modules so feature teams can request Postgres without clicking through the DigitalOcean UI. Hiring to strengthen day-to-day IaC for managed databases and safe plan-before-apply habits.
day_to_day: Author and review OpenTofu for DigitalOcean managed databases and related cloud resources
Keep provider versions and variables clear so others can init and plan the same stack
Validate changes with tofu plan before anyone applies to shared accounts
Pair with backend engineers on “what would this create?” reviews of database sizing and region choices
Improve shared templates and conventions for managed Postgres on DigitalOcean
required_skills: Comfortable writing OpenTofu (or Terraform-compatible) HCL with required_providers and provider blocks
Can declare a DigitalOcean managed Postgres cluster (digitalocean_database_cluster with engine pg)
Can pass a DigitalOcean API token via variable or environment without committing secrets
Can run tofu init and tofu plan and interpret a create plan
nice_to_have_skills: Familiarity with DigitalOcean database size slugs and regions
Experience with remote state backends and workspaces
Prior work on internal platform or developer-experience IaC modules
Knowledge of database firewalls, replicas, or connection pooling on DigitalOcean
constraints: Assessment focuses on OpenTofu that would create a managed Postgres cluster — not applying it live or operating an existing cluster
Do not test Kubernetes, multi-cloud sprawl, or full VPC networking in this challenge
Candidate works in a desktop environment with Terminal and OpenTofu available; they bring their own DigitalOcean API token
Requirements on the desktop are shared scenery; do not replace the target with a different cloud or database product

rubric.name: Successful dry-run
rubric.summary: Shows a successful tofu plan that would create the managed Postgres cluster.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Did the candidate demonstrate a successful tofu plan (exit success) for their OpenTofu config that plans creation of a DigitalOcean managed Postgres cluster? Answer YES only if video or narrative shows plan completing successfully (create planned for the database cluster). Plan failure, apply-as-completion, or inferred “probably works” = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Correct Postgres cluster config
rubric.summary: Declares a DigitalOcean managed Postgres cluster with engine, size, region, version, and node count matching the spec.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Does the deliverable declare digitalocean_database_cluster (or equivalent DO managed DB resource) with engine pg and name, region, size, version, and node_count matching the instance requirements on the desktop? Answer YES only if engine is Postgres and the required parameters match the scenery. Wrong engine, wrong cloud, or mismatched required params = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Secrets and dry-run discipline
rubric.summary: Supplies the API token via environment or sensitive vars, and finishes with plan only—no live apply.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Is the DigitalOcean token supplied via environment variable and/or a sensitive variable / non-committed tfvars pattern (not hardcoded in .tf left on the desktop), and is completion path plan-only (no evidence that apply / live cluster creation was required to finish)? Answer YES only if both secrets hygiene and plan-only discipline hold. Hardcoded token in deliverable files or apply treated as the required finish = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Clarity of deliverables
rubric.summary: Leaves OpenTofu files a reviewer can init and plan without guessing layout or undocumented steps.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Are OpenTofu .tf files left on the desktop that a reviewer could init and plan without guessing paths or undocumented steps? Answer YES if the primary module is present and self-explanatory enough to dry-run; optional notes must be accurate if present. No .tf / cannot plan from the workspace = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.
